Quarantine ME
​
SECTION A: SYNOPSIS
Spoiler
Quarantine ME
is an immersive narrative adventure that challenges your perceptions and intuition. Trapped in a room that changes and transforms every day, explore a surreal world where every choice you make alters the course of the story. With over 100 possible endings and gameplay that evolves based on your decisions, every playthrough is unique and engaging. Prepare for a deep and introspective experience where the true adversary is your own psyche. Escape the quarantine and discover what awaits you outside!
IMAGES/SCREENSHOTS
Spoiler
(These are optional)
SECTION B: CHARACTERS
Spoiler
Main character is YOU.
SECTION C: STORYLINE/PLOT
Spoiler
A lonely creature has to stay quarantined in a room a few days for its best.
CREDITS (work in progress): Music are from Ricky Z (that uses over 20pseudo), most of the scripts are from Galv. Everything else is me (graphics, text, idk). I am missing a few scripts not from Galv but atm I'm not sure I've used that in the game (even if they might appear inside the demo, I might soon remove 'em from the game).
SECTION D: SETTING AND/OR WORLD DEVELOPMENT
Spoiler
1 character, 1 room, 10 days.
DOWNLOAD LINK
Spoiler
Q.ME: Path F [Demo]
This is not a video game.
It is not designed to entertain you, nor to amuse you.
It is a tool for assessment: a slow, imperfect, and at times uncomfortable exploration of how you react, choose, and relate to the unknown.
This demo contains only Path F — one of the 12 routes planned for the full version.
Even within this excerpt, there are nearly 15 possible endings to discover, while the complete game will feature over 100 different endings.
As a demo and a work in progress, some feedback may feel imprecise or partial: Path F is intended for those who feel the need to take care of something, but it might not be the ideal path for every type of player.
We invite you to experience it for what it is: an inner journey, not a consumer product.
If you are looking for a video game, this is not for you.
If you are looking for yourself, you might be in the right place.

PATH F EXPLANATION:
F stands for flower. This path is dedicated to those who explore the process of becoming, here indicated by the plant growth and its chance to bloom into a flower or wither / get eaten.
What's your idea of supporting growth? Is it to take care or to protect? Take care and Protect are two different paths and your choices will affect the plant health differently according to your meaning of supporting growth.
On D6F you will discover that the plant is rotting and withering (W path) or being attacked by some kind of weird parasites (P path). Again, your choices will affect the plant differently according to the path you've found yourself in.
It will be progressively questioned whether it's right to interfere with the growth or it would be better to just observe it.
On D7F you'll discover that the rot and parasites are growing as well and that supporting the plant growth will mean to disrupt the rot and parasites growth. Will you still support the plant or will you cheer for the rot/parasites?
On D8F your actions will result in the plant blooming into a complete flower, withering and rotting, or getting completely eaten by a flourishing parasite colony.
HOW TO ACCESS:
having a high K stat and taking a non-conformist (do the opposite of what the sign says) and non-linear (exit left) choice during the D4 Bonus Stage.
RELEASE:
D6FW is ready and will be published in a few hours, complete F path is expected to be ready at early September
"It's up to you and any choice is fine, my little one"
Images: D6FW

posts.author: hiddenone
posts.body:
Heyas, I gave your demo a try and I just want to say off the bat that this was not a game for me. I know you say that this isn't a game and shouldn't entertain or amuse the player, but I play games to have fun... And this felt like I was sitting through a psych lecture. I want to be clear that doesn't make this bad or anything like that, it just means it wasn't my type of game.
Spoiler:
Feedback
Since this isn't my type of game I'm not going to focus on the plot or the choices. The concept of every choice affecting the room and the ending is interesting, and I assume that for the players that do enjoy this it really is a lot of fun to see how each choice splits the timeline. The custom art did a good job of showing changes every day, though I wasn't always sure why certain changes happened.
I do think you could polish the presentation, both with how the dialogue is shown and the writing itself. Having ME's dialogue appear above its head works fine (except when it's hidden behind the UI), but the Narrator's messages would appear almost randomly. Sometimes it was near the bottom of the screen, sometimes it was near the top, sometimes it covered up ME. While it would take a lot of adjustments on your part, I almost feel like having the Narrator's message box always visible at the bottom of the screen would be more impactful. Have it be part of the UI, and display the Narrator's dialogue only there. And when the Narrator abandons ME, remove the message box so that the player really feels that they've been left all alone.
The writing is flowery to its own detriment. I could follow what the Narrator was saying, but it would take its time and repeat itself in ways that reminded me of that "people die when they are killed" anime meme. It would really be worth it to you to hire an English editor to help smooth out the awkward phrases and make it all flow better. And I'm not sure, but did you want the Narrator to be so antagonistic to ME? It felt like the Narrator hated ME and went out of its way to insult ME for my choices. Like for the choice where I could choose why I wanted the flower to bloom I chose "beautiful" since I don't see flowers as "fragile", and the Narrator went off about how I chose the least meaningful option and that I clearly don't look beyond the surface of things. That's the point where I mostly disengaged with the game, since it made me think that no matter what choices I make the Narrator will attack me for them. If you wanted the Narrator to be cruel when talking to ME, you've succeeded, but if that wasn't your aim then I think it needs a major rewrite.
I ended up getting the Patient Observer ending, meaning I became Charles Darwin? I'm honestly not sure how I got an ending about observing since I really tried to go out of my way to not observe the parasites and the rest of the room after the first few days just to see what would happen if I didn't do much. I'm sure there is reasoning to all the possible endings, but the ending I got just didn't feel like it reflected how I was playing.
There were a few other bugs and oddities:
Black text on a grey background is hard to read, if your tutorials are important make sure there's enough contrast to be easy of your player's eyes. It seemed to only happen once in a while, so double-check your events
The message box goes behind the UI, meaning it can be hidden depending on where the MC stands
When the flower is being attacked, the choice window is for the Narrator, not the MC's. The wrong window for the current speaker does appear randomly throughout the game
Part of the letters are cut off when the Narrator is speaking, mostly ones like 'y' or 'g'
At the start of each day the camera zooms in twice on the MC, and then the cutscene starts
[/SPOILER]
Overall, you clearly have a vision for this game even if it's not something I enjoyed. I think you've made it difficult for yourself since there are so many possible routes and endings, so make sure that you go through and polish every bit of dialogue and choice so that players can feel the consequences of their choices and it doesn't feel too random.
Good luck with your project!

This is great feedback, I'll treasure it and try to reward the time you dedicated to it.
q.ME is a project I worked on for am year in an echo-chamber, the demo you played (demoF I guess) has about 2500window box and is almost 1yr old. After releasing it I've got a lot of feedback, so I took a break and I'm now reworking it.
I apologize for it being not fun, but it wasn't meant to be fun. I hoped the whole alternative/feedback concept was at least enjoyable, but it's not and I'm strugglin finding a way to fix it. I fear there are none but if you have any I'll glady hear.
I'm english second language, I tried to keep the language simple but I know there are many typos and such. I'm now using DeepL and Gpt to fix dialogues, I dislike AI but it's the best tool I have for translation.
About the message box: Galv var bar stands above text. I edited it, so the next version it wont cover msg box. The idea to use narrator (I call it TheRoom) text in a box below is great, I'll implement it. The cut Y and G is an error due to the font I think, so I doubt I can solve it (but I can chamge the font)
The Darwin ending: It's great you noticed it belongs to Darwin. That happens of you get the parasite path, of yoy care about parasites, if thwy survive. You are also a good/positive person (another ending possible in that path is Mendel or Lucrezia Borgia iirc).
About the random changes: this not-game is meant to be a projective test. It means that the pazient/user should not know the meaning of everything, a guide for therapist is meant to be available in combo. It's exagerately optimistic but this is meant to be played in therapy before the first session. Most of the alternatives are cut out in the demo, there will be 12 (8?) different path and 100 endings while in this demo it s narrowed to 15.
The zoom: it happens twice because the first one is for dialogue while the second one is to see how the shape of the main char has changed. It's not meant to happen twice actually so I'll look into that.
About your feedback: I rly dig into that. I'm now working at a 2nd project that will hopwfully keep what s good in q.me and also try to push what I ve learned abput RPGmaker/aseprite/mygamejampartecipations. Finding some good feedback is tough, so I hope we can connect so I you can feedback me on next projects before I release em.
About TheRoom: dialogues have alternatives, those ain't perfect but they often take in consideration your Goodness stat. positive (5+) stat will lead to much more positiv feedback, lower one will indicate a conflict brtween you and the room.
The Plot: q.ME focus on fetuses early abilities (according to my profession). In a v.game context, it's the fetus deciding his context.That why I used 9days (months). It also follows a deterministic, but optimistic, way to see it: once you're born your future is all written in an historical character comparison
TL;DR : q.ME is a p ojwct developed in an echo-chamber. It has flaws and that s why I m totally reworking it. It s not meant to be fun be neither a pain.

AI 'helping' with the dialogue actually explains a lot, I think it's doing your writing dirty. A lot of the phrases were technically correct, but the emotion and feeling behind them wasn't coming through and I think the game suffers because of that. There's a lot of dialogue in this story so I know that it feels overwhelming to go through it all, but some more polish and tweaking of sentences would significantly improve the game without having to fully redo the whole thing.
A machine translation is a quick way to get the dialogue into English, but having a human editor will make sure that the care you put into the original Italian will also be there in the English version.
